claims.text: West Texas A&M University received a $9.75 million grant from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which the A&M System release calls the largest federal award in University history.
claims.quote: West Texas A&M University has received a $9.75 million grant from the U.S. Department of Agriculture—the largest federal award in University history
claims.document: Texas A&M University System press release, October 7th, 2026

claims.text: The release says the USDA awarded the grant through its Research Facilities Act Program for a center for beef cattle research and innovation.
claims.quote: awarded the grant for a center for beef cattle research and innovation through its Research Facilities Act Program
claims.document: Texas A&M University System press release, October 7th, 2026
claims.note: The release names the agency National Institute for Food and Agriculture. Do not print that name. NIFA's own pages returned 503.

claims.text: A required dollar-for-dollar match of $4.875 million from the Texas A&M University System and $4.875 million from other sources brings the project total to $19.5 million, according to the release.

claims.document: Texas A&M University System press release, October 7th, 2026

claims.text: The research feedlot will pair 90 small research pens for scientific studies with 45 commercial-scale pens.
claims.quote: by pairing 90 small research pens for scientific studies with 45 commercial-scale pens
claims.document: Texas A&M University System press release, October 7th, 2026

claims.text: Plans for the research feedlot include a precision beef cattle handling facility, a veterinary care and research hospital, an advanced technology feed and production center and a metabolism and physiology center.

claims.document: Texas A&M University System press release, October 7th, 2026

claims.text: The release says new feeding, health and handling techniques can be evaluated with traditional and artificial intelligence-powered approaches.

claims.text: The A&M System release of October 7th, 2026 names no AI tool, vendor, camera, model or result. Its only mention of artificial intelligence is a planned way of evaluating techniques.
claims.quote: artificial intelligence-powered approaches that are designed to increase beef production efficiency and advance feedlot management practices
claims.document: Texas A&M University System press release, October 7th, 2026
